name: [rail-archiver] Feed went dark
message:
Feed `{{feed.name}}` (normal cadence) has emitted no polls for ~90 minutes. Slow feeds (interval_class:slow, e.g. Bay Area 511) are covered separately by `Slow feed went dark`.

NOTE on the 90-min window: this monitor fires on no-data, and the window is deliberately long (not 15 min). A feed that fails repeatedly is *quarantined* and dropped to an hourly fallback poll — it is NOT dark, just degraded, and is covered by the `Feed quarantined` monitor. A 30-min no-data window flapped on that hourly cadence (alert → next poll lands → recover → repeat). 90 min clears the 60-min quarantine cadence, so this monitor now means "genuinely producing nothing," and a fast feed that dies abruptly is still caught within minutes by `Feed quarantined` (5 consecutive failures).

Most common causes:
- Upstream URL changed (check agency dev portal)
- API key expired (check `.env`)
- DNS / network issue

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs --since 2h | grep {{feed.name}}
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Batch step errored in last 24h
query: sum(last_1d):default_zero(sum:rollup.day.duration.count{env:prod, service:rail-archiver, status:error}.as_count()) + default_zero(sum:ship.cold.duration.count{env:prod, service:rail-archiver, status:error}.as_count()) + default_zero(sum:ship.hot.duration.count{env:prod, service:rail-archiver, status:error}.as_count()) > 0
message:
One or more batch operations (rollup or ship) failed in the last 24h.

Total errors across rollup.day + ship.cold + ship.hot: {{value}}

Each term is wrapped in `default_zero()` on purpose: a `status:error` series only exists on a day that step failed, and Datadog arithmetic with a missing series returns no data. Without it this fired only when all three failed on the same day.

Investigate:
```
aws logs tail /ecs/rail-archiver-rollup --since 24h | grep -iE 'error|traceback'
```

Rollup and ship now run as a daily ECS task, not on the box (hence the CloudWatch log group above). This is a once-a-day batch — a single failure can lose a day's worth of S3 uploads if not retried.

name: [rail-archiver] Schema drift detected
message:
Decoder schema drift detected on feed `{{feed.name}}` — the incoming payload is missing required keys, so its records are being dropped from the rollup.

Most common causes:
- Upstream agency renamed or removed a JSON key
- The decoder's `required_input_keys` is out of date relative to the live API

Investigate:
```
grep drift_missing_required archive/{{feed.name}}/metadata/year=*/month=*/day=*/data.jsonl | tail
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Poller heartbeat absent
message:
Poller shard `{{shard.name}}` on `{{host.name}}` has emitted no `poller.heartbeat` in the last 5 minutes — that process is down or hung.

Grouped by host and shard: every shard on every regional box sends its own heartbeat, so one dead shard is caught even while the others keep running (an ungrouped average stayed at 1 until *every* poller died). Unlike `Feed went dark` (which is per-feed), this is the unambiguous "this poller is not running" alert. An 18h outage once went unnoticed because nothing watched for this.

Most common causes:
- Poller container crashed and is crash-looping (check `restart` count)
- Poller hung mid-request (autoheal should have restarted it — check why it didn't)
- datadog-agent down, so the heartbeat never reached Datadog

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml ps
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs app-shard-{{shard.name}} --since 15m
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Poll error rate elevated
query: avg(last_30m):( sum:feed.poll.duration.count{env:prod, service:rail-archiver, status:error}.as_count() / sum:feed.poll.duration.count{env:prod, service:rail-archiver}.as_count() ) * 100 > 5
message:
Poll error rate is {{value}}% across all feeds over the last 30 minutes.

Counts both transport failures (no HTTP response) and HTTP >= 400 responses, which are tagged `status:error` with `error_type:HTTP<code>`, the same line backoff/quarantine uses. A single failing feed does NOT go dark (it keeps polling, just with errors). It gets quarantined after 5 consecutive failures, so see `Feed quarantined` for per-feed problems. If this fires on its own, suspect a systemic issue:
- Outbound network from the container
- DNS resolver
- Auth refresh logic
- Or a transient where many agencies' feeds are down at once (not unusual on weekends)

Drill in:
- Dashboard "Rail Archiver — Pipeline Health" → row 2 → "Poll errors by feed and error_type"

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Feed quarantined (dead feed)
message:
Feed `{{feed.name}}` has been QUARANTINED after repeated consecutive failures — the poller gave up on its normal cadence and dropped it to a long fallback interval (~1h), so it is effectively producing no fresh data until it recovers.

This alert stays open for as long as the feed is quarantined: it is driven by the `feed.quarantine_state` gauge (1 while quarantined, re-sent every 60s), and it resolves only when a poll succeeds and the gauge drops to 0. A poller restart also clears it, because quarantine state is in-memory; a still-dead feed re-quarantines after 5 more failures.

Unlike a transient blip, quarantine means the feed failed K times in a row. Most common causes:
- Upstream URL changed or the endpoint was retired (check the agency dev portal)
- API key expired or revoked (check `.env`)
- Agency is down for an extended window

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs --since 2h | grep -i 'quarantined\|{{feed.name}}'
tail archive/{{feed.name}}/metadata/year=*/month=*/day=*/data.jsonl
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Archiver internal error
message:
An UNEXPECTED exception fired inside `archive_one` for feed `{{feed.name}}` ({{value}} in 30m).

This is NOT a transport/HTTP failure — those are caught and recorded as TransportErrorResponse and surface via `Feed went dark` / `Poll error rate`. A `poll.error` means something archiver-side broke: a parsing/writing bug, or a local-disk / write-path failure (disk full, permissions). The self-protecting `_on_done` keeps the loop alive, but this poll's data may have been lost.

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs --since 30m | grep -A20 'unexpected error polling'
df -h   # rule out a full disk on the write path
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Slow feed went dark
message:
Slow-cadence feed `{{feed.name}}` has not polled in the last 90 minutes. These feeds (interval_class:slow) poll every ~17-30 min by design — often because they share a rate-limited key (e.g. Bay Area 511 at 60 req/hr) — so they get a longer dark window than normal feeds. 90 min with zero polls means it is genuinely stuck, not just slow.

Most common causes:
- Upstream URL changed or endpoint retired
- Shared API key expired/revoked (one bad key darkens the whole agency)
- The agency's rate budget is so saturated the feed never wins a token (check `poll.rate_limited` on the dashboard)

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs --since 2h | grep {{feed.name}}
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Ingest saturated (polls being shed)
message:
Box `{{host.name}}` shed {{value}} polls to the concurrency gate (`poll.skipped`) in the last 15 min — every worker slot on THAT box was busy, so feeds were skipped rather than queued. Grouped by host (since the regional poller expansion) so this names the specific box instead of a fleet-wide total that hides which one is actually struggling.

With the startup herd fixed (seed spread), steady-state poll.skipped should be ~0. Sustained shedding means the box can't keep up: polls are taking longer than expected, or there are simply too many feeds for the worker pool.

NOTE: this threshold (100/15m) is a first guess with no baseline yet — tune it against the dashboard once you've watched normal load. This is a CAPACITY signal, not an outage: data isn't lost, but coverage is thinning.

Levers:
- Raise `--workers` (more concurrent polls)
- Lengthen poll intervals on low-value feeds
- Shard feeds across processes (roadmap step 4)

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Feed poll overrunning its interval
message:
Feed `{{feed.name}}` is still processing a previous poll when its next one comes due (`poll.overrun`) -- {{value}} times in the last 15 min. The per-feed concurrency guard (main.py) sheds these cycles rather than letting a second `archive_one()` for the same feed start while the first is still in flight, so no duplicate work happens -- but it does mean this feed is effectively polling slower than its configured `poll_interval_seconds`.

This is exactly the signature the DELFI feed (`GTFS_DE_DELFI_REALTIME_DATA`, currently disabled in feeds.yaml) produced before it started OOM-crash-looping the EU box: an unusually large or slow feed whose fetch+decode+write routinely outruns its own poll interval.

This is a NEW metric (added alongside the guard) with no baseline yet -- tune the threshold (5/15m) once you've watched normal load.

Levers:
- Raise the feed's `poll_interval_seconds` in `config/feeds.yaml` to something it can actually keep up with
- Give it its own shard via `shard_pin` if it's dragging down other feeds sharing its worker pool (see `archiver/shard.py`)
- Investigate why the poll itself is slow: payload size, decode cost, the BatchingWriter's per-window buffer, or the hourly S3 merge

name: [rail-archiver] TLS cert expiring or expired
message:
Agency `{{agency.name}}`'s TLS certificate is at {{value}} days remaining (negative = already expired).

Emitted daily by `cert_check.py`, which probes each agency's HTTPS endpoint out-of-band (independent of `tls_verify`, so it sees the cert even on feeds where we've disabled verification). An expired cert breaks the poller's verified HTTPS and the feed goes dark — this is exactly how TRI_RAIL lost 8 days before this monitor existed.

Act before it hits zero:
- Most agencies auto-renew; if one lapses, contact them.
- Stopgap to keep collecting through a lapse: set `tls_verify: false` on the agency in `config/feeds.yaml` (only acceptable for no-auth feeds — it disables MITM protection).

RECOVERY: when the agency renews, `days_remaining` jumps back up and this monitor clears on its own — that recovery notification is your cue to flip any `tls_verify: false` back to true.

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] TLS verification disabled but cert is healthy
message:
Agency `{{agency.name}}` has `tls_verify: false` in `config/feeds.yaml`, but its TLS certificate is currently healthy ({{value}} days remaining). The reason to disable verification — an expired or broken cert — no longer applies, so the feed is polling without MITM protection for no benefit.

Action: flip `tls_verify` back to `true` for this agency and let verified HTTPS resume. Then this clears.

This is the recovery half of the cert lifecycle: it catches a feed you patched with `tls_verify: false` once its cert is valid again (e.g. the agency renewed, or you set it preemptively and the expiry you feared never happened). The 21-day floor (vs the 14-day expiry warning) is intentional hysteresis so a cert hovering near expiry doesn't flap between the two monitors.

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Host disk usage high
message:
Poller box `{{host.name}}`'s root filesystem is {{value}}% full.

Covers every poller box (`host:rail-archiver*` = rail-archiver, rail-archiver-eu, rail-archiver-au). All three run the same AL2023 arm64 AMI with a single root EBS volume, so `/dev/nvme0n1p1` is the root device on each.

`system.disk.in_use` is the Datadog Agent's default `disk` check — no custom instrumentation needed, it was already running (confirmed 2026-08-20: matches `df -h /` exactly, since the agent container's own overlay root lives on the same volume as the host — there's no separate data disk on this box). This alert just didn't exist before 2026-08-20 — the local landing zone (raw window `.bin` files plus the local-only daily `data.jsonl`, see `landing_layout.py`) grew unbounded for weeks with nothing watching disk size or pruning it, and the box went down when it filled.

Most common causes:
- `rail-archiver-prune.timer` stopped firing or is erroring (check `journalctl -u rail-archiver-prune.service`) — it only deletes a day-partition once its cold tarball is confirmed in S3, so a stuck/failing ship path silently blocks pruning too
- A single feed producing abnormally large raw payloads (e.g. `gtfs-de-delfi-realtime-data-trips-alerts`, a nationwide feed with ~150-200MB per 5-min window) outgrowing the 3-day buffer
- Docker image/log buildup unrelated to the landing zone

Investigate:
```
df -h /
du -sh /opt/rail-archiver/archive/*/ | sort -rh | head -20
journalctl -u rail-archiver-prune.service --no-pager | tail -60
docker system df
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Landing raw windows not shipping to S3
message:
The oldest raw window on `{{host.name}}` shard `{{shard.name}}` has been closed for {{value}}s without reaching the S3 landing.

`landing.raw_oldest_unshipped_age_s` is gauged once per raw ship pass (hourly) by the LandingUploader. Normal is under ~2h (one ship window plus grace). Anything older means windows are failing to ship. They are not lost: the uploader sweeps every on-disk day until a pass succeeds, and local prune (`prune.skipped_unshipped_windows`) refuses to delete a day that still has unshipped windows. The cost is disk: those days stay on the box until they ship, so a long backlog leads to `Host disk usage high`.

Most common causes:
- Expired or rotated AWS creds / IAM change on the poller box
- Regional S3 outage
- Box was down and is still catching up (the value should fall on its own within a pass or two)

NO DATA (no reading for 4h): the uploader on this shard stopped reporting at all. If `Poller heartbeat absent` is also firing, the whole shard is down. If not, the poll loop is alive but the LandingUploader is stuck or crashed, and nothing is shipping.

Investigate:
```
docker compose -f compose.prod.yml logs --since 3h | grep -i 'raw window upload failed\|oldest unshipped'
journalctl -u rail-archiver-prune.service --no-pager | grep 'not yet shipped'
```

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Daily rollup task did not run
message:
No `rollup.day` metric for 28 hours: the nightly rollup ECS task (rollup + gtfs + gold + ship via `pipeline/agency_batch.py`) has not rolled up a single feed-day since yesterday.

`rollup.day` is emitted per feed-day whether the rollup succeeds or fails (failures surface via `Batch step errored`), so silence means the task never started or died before rolling anything up:
- The EventBridge schedule `rail-archiver-rollup-daily` is disabled, or the nightly state machine (stage split) didn't invoke it
- ECS couldn't place the task (capacity, image pull, or secrets errors)
- The task was OOM-killed early
- The datadog-agent sidecar was down, so no metric left the task

Investigate:
```
aws scheduler get-schedule --name rail-archiver-rollup-daily --query State
aws ecs list-tasks --cluster rail-archiver --desired-status STOPPED
aws logs tail /ecs/rail-archiver-rollup --since 30h
```

This only alerts on silence: the `< 1` threshold never trips while the job is healthy, and `no_data_timeframe` (28h = one nightly run plus slack) does the work. (It watches `rollup.day` rather than `pipeline.task.duration` because the latter was never reaching Datadog: the task's EXIT trap sent it after the drain sleep.)

@<your-notification-target>

name: [rail-archiver] Daily cert check did not run
message:
No `cert.days_remaining` reading from any agency for 28 hours: the daily `cert_check` ECS task is not producing data.

While this fires, BOTH TLS monitors are blind: they don't alert on missing data, so a cert could lapse unnoticed (TRI_RAIL lost 8 days this way).

Most common causes:
- The EventBridge schedule `rail-archiver-cert-check-daily` is disabled (`cert_check_schedule_enabled` defaults to false in terraform/variables.tf)
- The task fails before emitting (it runs under `set -e`)
- ECS couldn't place the task, or the datadog-agent sidecar was down

Investigate:
```
aws scheduler get-schedule --name rail-archiver-cert-check-daily --query State
aws logs tail /ecs/rail-archiver-cert-check --since 30h
```

This only alerts on silence: the `< -36500` threshold (a cert 100 years expired) never trips, and `no_data_timeframe` (28h) does the work.
